reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getScheduleAmount and threads the op through its callers, but re-derives the 7.5% tolerance inline instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.ts, which defines the matching tolerance.

duplication.why: `Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075)` copies getApproxNumberThreshold, so the tolerance used for planning and for matching can now drift apart.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts getScheduleAmount, and callers only pass their own op field.

scope.why: Only the helper, its four callers, the raw type and a test change.

maintainability.why: One optional op parameter is a clean extension; the duplicated tolerance constant is the one thing a maintainer would have to keep in sync.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduleAmount computes the approx tolerance itself instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts).

disguised_duplication.where: The tolerance expression is copied verbatim from getApproxNumberThreshold, not disguised.

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduleAmount(amount, op), used by api-models.ts, forecast-schedules.ts, schedules/app.ts (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule) and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions; the budget template and client getScheduledAmount never used the worst-case rule in this tree.
